claims.text: The Coral Triangle holds at least 500 species of reef-building coral in each of its ecoregions, the richest reefs anywhere.
claims.evidenceNote: The scenery draws this as an illustration: shapes and colours suggest the place, they are not a survey of it.

claims.text: Acropora corals, which include table, elkhorn and staghorn corals, are spread across the Indo-Pacific with over 100 species, and the Caribbean with three.
claims.evidenceNote: The scenery draws this as an illustration: shapes and colours suggest the place, they are not a survey of it.

claims.text: The Red Sea's extensive shallow shelves have more than 200 kinds of soft and hard coral, and its reefs are among the healthiest in the world.
claims.evidenceNote: The scenery draws this as an illustration: shapes and colours suggest the place, they are not a survey of it.

claims.text: Atolls such as the Chagos and the Maldives are low-lying rings of islands set around lagoons.
claims.evidenceNote: The scenery draws this as an illustration: shapes and colours suggest the place, they are not a survey of it.

claims.text: The Seychelles sit atop a large submerged block of granite, a fragment of Gondwana between Madagascar and India.
claims.evidenceNote: The scenery draws this as an illustration: shapes and colours suggest the place, they are not a survey of it.

claims.text: Many of these islands are volcanic: exposed peaks of undersea mountain ranges built by volcanic activity.
claims.evidenceNote: The scenery draws this as an illustration: shapes and colours suggest the place, they are not a survey of it.

claims.text: The Hawaiian Islands are eight major volcanic islands, the exposed peaks of an undersea mountain range; the yellow tang was first described from fish collected there.
claims.evidenceNote: The scenery draws this as an illustration: shapes and colours suggest the place, they are not a survey of it. The yellow school is drawn as yellow tang only at Hawaii.

claims.text: Rapa Nui is a volcanic island on the Salas y Gómez Ridge, a mostly submarine mountain range of seamounts formed by a hotspot.
claims.evidenceNote: The scenery draws this as an illustration: shapes and colours suggest the place, they are not a survey of it.

claims.text: The Canary Islands are volcanic; Lanzarote, the easternmost, shows evidence of recent volcanic activity.
claims.evidenceNote: The scenery draws this as an illustration: shapes and colours suggest the place, they are not a survey of it.

claims.text: Cape Verde is ten volcanic islands, made mostly of igneous rock and pyroclastic debris.
claims.evidenceNote: The scenery draws this as an illustration: shapes and colours suggest the place, they are not a survey of it.

claims.text: Elkhorn coral, a branching coral whose many branches resemble elk antlers, is an important reef builder in the Caribbean; turtle grass forms meadows in calm, shallow, sandy water across the Caribbean.
claims.evidenceNote: The scenery draws this as an illustration: shapes and colours suggest the place, they are not a survey of it.

claims.text: Off the Florida Keys, sand ridges are covered by large beds of seagrass with patch reefs scattered across them.
claims.evidenceNote: The scenery draws this as an illustration: shapes and colours suggest the place, they are not a survey of it.

claims.text: Turtle grass grows in meadows in calm, shallow, sandy water throughout the Caribbean Sea and the Gulf of Mexico.
claims.evidenceNote: The scenery draws this as an illustration: shapes and colours suggest the place, they are not a survey of it.

claims.text: Bermuda is known for pink sand beaches and clear, blue water, and for reefs and wrecks in shallow water with virtually unlimited visibility.
claims.evidenceNote: The scenery draws this as an illustration: shapes and colours suggest the place, they are not a survey of it.

claims.text: The Gulf of California has three general types of shore: rocky shore, sandy beach and tidal flat. Sargassum, a brown seaweed, is widespread in tropical and subtropical seas.
claims.evidenceNote: The scenery draws this as an illustration: shapes and colours suggest the place, they are not a survey of it. Brown algae here are drawn as Sargassum-like clumps, not identified to species.

claims.text: Neptune grass (Posidonia oceanica) is a seagrass found only in the Mediterranean, one of the most nutrient-poor seas in the world.
claims.evidenceNote: The scenery draws this as an illustration: shapes and colours suggest the place, they are not a survey of it.

claims.text: The Persian Gulf is very shallow: at most about 90 m deep and about 50 m on average.
claims.evidenceNote: The scenery draws this as an illustration: shapes and colours suggest the place, they are not a survey of it.

claims.text: Mauritius is surrounded by white sandy beaches, and its lagoons are protected from the open sea by one of the largest coral reefs in the world.
claims.evidenceNote: The scenery draws this as an illustration: shapes and colours suggest the place, they are not a survey of it.

claims.text: Ningaloo Reef is Australia's largest fringing coral reef, and the only large reef positioned very close to a landmass.
claims.evidenceNote: The scenery draws this as an illustration: shapes and colours suggest the place, they are not a survey of it.

claims.text: The islands of Okinawa are surrounded by some of the most abundant coral reefs in the world.
claims.evidenceNote: The scenery draws this as an illustration: shapes and colours suggest the place, they are not a survey of it.

claims.text: The tiger cowrie is found at depths of 10 to 40 metres, often with live coral such as table-forming Acropora.
claims.evidenceNote: Wikipedia cites FAO for the depth range.

claims.text: The money cowrie lives in intertidal rocky areas and shallow tide pools, on and under rocks in shallow water and on reefs exposed at low tide.
claims.evidenceNote: No depth in metres is given, so the simulator draws it in the shallowest water and says so.

claims.text: The textile cone is found in estuaries, on rocky shores and in rock pools; by day it is usually buried in sand, and it emerges to feed at night.
claims.evidenceNote: No depth in metres is given, so the simulator draws it in shallow water and says so.

claims.text: Nautiluses usually live several hundred metres down; equatorial populations are usually deeper than 100 m, and only around New Caledonia, the Loyalty Islands and Vanuatu are they seen as shallow as 5 m. Their shells are thought to implode around 800 m.
claims.evidenceNote: Depth ranges vary between populations; the simulator draws the deep range except at Vanuatu and New Caledonia.

claims.text: Water absorbs red light first, which is why it looks blue; sunlight reaches down only through the photic zone, roughly the top 200 metres, below which there is little light.
claims.evidenceNote: Used to tint and darken the scene with depth; the exact colours are illustrative.

claims.text: Each place's water colour, the colour cast on everything in it and its sand are matched to underwater photographs taken there, from Wikimedia Commons: the median colour of open water in each photo, the average colour of the whole frame, and pale sand where it shows. Only colour statistics are used; places with few usable photos borrow from places with the same kind of reef. The list of photos, authors and licences for every place is in data/place-colours.json.
claims.evidenceNote: Photos vary with camera, lens, depth, light and editing, so these are a typical look, not a measurement of the water. Photos lit by a flash or taken out of the water were left out (data/research/place-photo-exclusions.json and the script's filters).
